header:
Date: 2025-06-12
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Finova Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (Finova Cloud Architect), Samir Verma (Finova DevOps), Jing Wei (Finova Compliance)
topics: In-transit TLS and mutual TLS options
Hardware Security Module (HSM) support and proofs
Audit logs and key access controls
transcript:
[00:00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run 45ish minutes, go over encryption at rest and our KMS options, and leave time for questions. Diego's going to lead the deep bits.
[00:00:12] Maya: Great, thanks. We care about BYOK and HSM, also proof that keys never leave our control. SOC2 is table stakes.
[00:00:20] Diego: Yep, understood. Quick intro: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. For encryption we do envelope encryption by default and integrate with customer KMS for DEK wrapping.
[00:00:35] Liam: When you say "integrate" — is that vault-based? Do you call AWS KMS, or can we use HashiCorp? We use HashiCorp Vault in prod.
[00:00:44] Diego: We have pluggable KMS adapters. Out-of-the-box we support AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault. For Private deployments you can bring your own HSM. For hosted we offer CMK-backed keys via customer-managed KMS where possible.
[00:00:58] Samir: Are keys ever stored in Redwood's environment unwrapped? That is a hard no on our side.
[00:01:05] Ava: Short answer: no. We store only wrapped DEKs; master keys (CMKs) remain in your KMS/HSM. We can do both symmetric and asymmetric depending on provider.
[00:01:15] Jing: Can you describe the envelope encryption flow from write to disk? We need to map this to our SOC2 controls.
[00:01:23] Diego: Sure. Rough flow: plaintext tokens -> generate DEK in memory -> encrypt with DEK -> DEK is wrapped by CMK via KMS call (Encrypt API) -> store ciphertext + wrapped DEK in object store. On read, unwrap DEK via KMS Decrypt, decrypt data in memory, stream out. KMS calls are logged and audited on the KMS side.
[00:01:46] Maya: Do you cache unwrapped DEKs in memory to reduce KMS calls? That can be a risk if memory persists or dumps happen.
[00:01:55] Diego: We have a configurable in-memory DEK cache with TTL and strict ACLs. For high-security customers we disable caching entirely, forcing a KMS unwrap per access. We also support hardware-backed key operations in the HSM path so the DEK never leaves HSM if you choose that model.
[00:02:12] Liam: For Private deployments, can we run Redwood control plane in our VPC and use CloudHSM? We need network isolation and to meet data residency.
[00:02:20] Ava: Yes — Redwood Private allows you to install a control plane into your VPC or on-prem. You can integrate with CloudHSM or a customer HSM appliance. The key material stays in your HSM.
[00:02:30] Samir: What about transit? Are we talking TLS 1.3 mutual TLS between services?
[00:02:35] Diego: We enforce TLS 1.3 for all in-transit. For Private we strongly recommend mutual TLS or VPC peering/PrivateLink. For hosted API calls, client->Redwood is TLS with optional mTLS for enterprise customers. Inter-service inside Redwood uses mTLS on dedicated/private clusters.
[00:02:50] Maya: Auditability: We need key usage logs that show which principal requested unwraps and when. Do you capture those events?
[00:02:58] Diego: On the KMS side, those logs are native — AWS CloudTrail, Google Cloud Audit Logs. We also produce our own audit logs showing which Redwood service account requested the unwrap, correlated with request IDs. We can push logs to your Log Destination (S3/GCS/ Splunk) or stream to your SIEM.
[00:03:15] Jing: Are those logs tamper-evident? We require retention and integrity checks.
[00:03:20] Ava: We can sign audit logs and support WORM storage for long-term retention. For high-assurance customers we recommend shipping logs to their own account bucket where they control lifecycle and retention policies.
[00:03:31] Liam: Key rotation — do you support automatic rotation of DEKs and re-wrapping with new CMKs? And can we schedule rekeying windows?
[00:03:40] Diego: Yes. DEKs are ephemeral and rotated per object/table by policy. For CMK rotation, if your KMS supports it, we can rewrap existing wrapped DEKs (we provide a rewrap job). We also support key versioning so you have a clear mapping from ciphertext to key version. Scheduling can be automated or manual.
[00:03:57] Maya: Does Redwood support BYOK — specifically customer-generated keys that never are exported? How do you handle import vs generate inside HSM?
[00:04:06] Diego: BYOK is supported. You can either import a key into your KMS/HSM or generate keys directly inside the HSM. In both cases the private key material never leaves your KMS/HSM if you keep it there. For hosted deployments we do a handshake where you establish a CMK under your account and grant Redwood's service principal Encrypt/Decrypt IAM permissions; we never export the key.
[00:04:26] Samir: You said HSM path — does that mean Redwood supports CloudHSM and on-prem Luna appliances?
[00:04:32] Diego: We support CloudHSM and common FIPS 140-2/3 HSM appliances via our Private deployment connectors. For on-prem, we integrate over a direct network connection with KMIP or vendor APIs.
[00:04:44] Maya: Any certification evidence for the HSM interactions? We need to show FIPS 140-2 level for some keys.
[00:04:50] Ava: We can share our integration matrices and vendor attestations. For CloudHSM you get vendor attestation; for appliances we map firmware versions and provide guidance. We'll include the relevant HSM compliance docs in the packet.
[00:05:02] Jing: How do you handle multi-tenant isolation for hosted customers that also use KMS? If multiple customers use the same Redwood hosted pool, can keys be cross-accessed?
[00:05:12] Diego: Isolation is strict. Each customer's wrapped DEKs are associated with their own CMK or a customer-specific key alias. Our service accounts never mix keys across tenants. For hosted, if you choose customer-managed key, the CMK is in your account, and Redwood only performs operations permitted by your IAM grants.
[00:05:26] Liam: Network egress concerns — when Redwood calls our KMS, is that a cross-account call? How do you authenticate?
[00:05:32] Diego: We use standard cloud auth patterns. For AWS, Redwood calls assume-role into a customer-provided role (you grant us a dedicated role) or you can use a cross-account CMK policy. For Vault, you can create a specific auth backend token with restricted policies. We document the recommended patterns.
[00:05:47] Maya: Is it possible to do a crypto-agile setup so we can swap KMS providers if needed without re-encrypting everything?
[00:05:53] Diego: We support key-translation patterns — you can rewrap DEKs from one CMK to another with a rewrap job. That avoids full re-encryption of all data payloads. Key versioning and metadata let you trace which CMK was used.
[00:06:05] Samir: What about data residency — if we require keys to be in EU and data to stay in EU, can Redwood guarantee that?
[00:06:12] Ava: Yes, with Dedicated or Private deployments, you can restrict region and keep keys in your EU KMS/HSM. For hosted, we have regional clusters; you can request EU-only tenancy and customer-managed keys in an EU account. We'll want to capture residency requirements in the contract.
[00:06:26] Jing: Regarding SSO/RBAC, can we restrict which Redwood engineers can request unwrap operations? We need least privilege for internal staff.
[00:06:34] Diego: Absolutely. On Dedicated/Private, you control the IAM roles and we integrate with your SSO/SAML. For hosted customers we enforce RBAC — operators have scoped roles and we can enable customer-managed approval workflows for critical actions. All unwrap requests are logged and are visible in the Console with the requesting principal.
[00:06:52] Maya: Pen tests and vulnerability assessments — will you allow us to include the KMS call paths in our pentest scope?
[00:07:00] Ava: Yes, we support coordinated Pentests with prior notice and scoping. For hosted customers, we have a process to coordinate and we can provide a test harness for KMS interactions.
[00:07:09] Liam: I want to go deeper on the HSM integration — can we walk through the sequence?
[00:07:14] Diego: Sure. Example: you deploy Redwood Private control plane into VPC. You provision a CloudHSM cluster or attach an on-prem HSM via a secure tunnel. CMK lives in HSM. When Redwood needs to wrap/unwrap, it makes an HSM operation via KMIP or vendor API; HSM returns key ops, never exporting private key material. Redwood logs the operation. We can configure FIPS ciphersuites and require key usage policies.
[00:07:40] Maya: Do you support offline key attestations, like providing signed statements of key origin for auditors?
[00:07:46] Diego: We can provide signed key attestations depending on your HSM vendor — some HSMs can produce signed attestations. For hosted we can provide vendor-signed certs and a chain of custody report. We'll detail the options in the doc.
[00:07:58] Jing: How about emergency key revocation/rekeying workflow? If we need to rotate or revoke CMK immediately, what is the impact on availability?
[00:08:06] Diego: If you revoke CMK policy or delete a key, unwraps will fail. We recommend a staged rekey: create new CMK, rewrap DEKs, then retire old CMK. For emergency scenarios, we support fallback policies that re-route to a compatibility CMK if preconfigured, but that needs to be set up in advance. Without a fallback, availability will be impacted.
[00:08:25] Samir: For compliance we need to show evidence of key rotation frequency and access logs for 2 years. Can Redwood help with log export/retention?
[00:08:33] Ava: Yes — we can stream logs to your storage with retention policies, and provide an audit export for the period you need. We also provide a Console view for quick export.
[00:08:42] Maya: Any limitations on crypto algorithms? We need RSA-PSS and AEAD ciphers like AES-GCM or AES-GCM-SIV.
[00:08:50] Diego: We support AEAD algorithms (AES-GCM), and for HSM-backed keys you get the vendor-supported algorithms. RSA operations are supported where the KMS supports them. We'll include an algorithm compatibility matrix.
[00:08:59] Liam: Can Redwood support customer side encryption for secret material before it hits Redwood? E.g., client-side encryption?
[00:09:04] Diego: You can do client-side encryption; Redwood will store the ciphertext as opaque blobs. That reduces functionality around search and tokenization, but it's supported.
[00:09:12] Ava: Quick recap of asks: Finova wants BYOK + HSM, log streaming to their SIEM, SOC2 docs, and a deep HSM/Terraform demo. We'll deliver those.
[00:09:21] Maya: Sounds good. A couple of gotchas: our compliance team will need the exact network flow diagram and the IAM role policies.
[00:09:27] Diego: We'll include a sample assume-role policy and least-privilege ACLs for Vault.
[00:09:32] Samir: Can you email an example of the DEK cache TTL config and disable switch? We might want to disable caching for PCI data.
[00:09:38] Ava: Will do — Diego will include config snippets.
[00:09:42] Jing: Also, we need the retention schedule for audit logs and how to prove immutability.
[00:09:47] Ava: We'll include WORM recommendations and S3 bucket policies.
[00:09:52] Liam: One last technical: latency impact of per-request unwrap — do you have SLO numbers?
[00:09:58] Diego: Typical KMS unwrap adds 30-120ms depending on region and HSM vs soft-KMS. Our envelope design keeps payload crypto local so the per-request cost is mainly the KMS roundtrip. We can run benchmarks in your region; that was one of the next steps.
[00:10:12] Maya: Ok, let's open to questions.
[00:10:15] Samir: In a DR event, can we recover keys if our HSM cluster fails?
[00:10:20] Diego: For CloudHSM you can configure multi-AZ clusters and snapshots. For on-prem HSMs, standard vendor DR patterns apply; we recommend a secondary HSM to be ready. We can assist with runbooks.
[00:10:34] Liam: Does Redwood keep any long-lived service account that can perform key ops without our explicit role?
[00:10:39] Ava: No — all key ops are performed by service principals that are scoped to your role; we don't store permanent credential material for customer KMS. We do have internal service identities, but they only operate under the permissions you grant and all actions are logged.
[00:10:53] Maya: Are we able to get a timeline estimate for Private deployment including HSM integration?
[00:10:58] Diego: Typical delivery for Private with HSM is 6-10 weeks after PO depending on network work and certs; we'll provide a more precise project plan in the follow-up.
[00:11:08] Ava: Ok, thanks everyone. We'll share docs and schedule the HSM deep dive week of 6/23.
[00:11:13] Maya: Thanks.
[00:11:15] [call continues with peripheral questions and wrap, approx. 40 more minutes of Q&A covering specific IAM snippets, Terraform examples, and compliance mapping — details in attachments to follow.]
